identity.title: Ascites exam: flank dullness, shifting dullness, fluid wave

technique.how: Supine patient: percuss from periumbilical tympany toward each flank to find flank dullness, then roll the patient toward one side and re-percuss for shifting of the dullness line. Fluid wave: place an assistant's hand edge on the midline, tap one flank sharply and feel for a transmitted impulse on the opposite flank.
technique.prerequisites: Supine and able to roll; empty bladder; expose the abdomen.
technique.contraindications: None absolute; avoid rolling with unstable spine or fresh laparotomy.

interpretation.positive_finding: Fluid wave (LR+ 9.6) and shifting dullness (LR+ 5.76) raise the probability of ultrasound-confirmed ascites; fluid wave is the more specific sign.
interpretation.negative_finding: No bulging flanks (LR- 0.12) or no flank dullness makes ascites unlikely; Cattau 1982 found absent flank dullness excluded ascites with >90% accuracy.
interpretation.pitfalls: Volumes under about 1 L are missed by percussion; obesity and gaseous distension confound; in patients with normal prothrombin time (low prevalence) positive signs were usually false positives.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: diagnostic paracentesis (SAAG, cell count; SBP work-up if febrile/AKI/AMS). Negative but concern persists: bedside ultrasound before abandoning the diagnosis.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a negative exam to exclude ascites when abdominal compartment syndrome, SBP or hepatorenal syndrome is being considered; image instead.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Tense ascites with hypotension, oliguria or respiratory compromise requires urgent paracentesis and assessment for abdominal compartment syndrome.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Cattau 1982: three independent examiners, overall accuracy only 58%; Simel 1988 reports LR ranges across examiners rather than single values.

extraction_notes: The 1992 RCE (PMID 1573754) has no PubMed abstract and no PMC text, so its pooled table could not be viewed; it is cited as the anchoring review but no number is taken from it. Numbers come from the abstract of Simel 1988 (the RCE's core primary study): LR+ fluid wave 9.6, LR+ shifting dullness 5.76, LR- absent bulging flanks 0.12; no CIs, sensitivity or specificity are given in the abstract, so those fields are null. Cattau 1982 (21 patients, 6 with ascites) reports only ranges (sens 50-94%, spec 29-82%) and that absent flank dullness excludes ascites with >90% accuracy - not entered as a per-sign estimate. Cummings 1985 reports positive predictive values (shifting dullness 51%, fluid wave 73%; 96% for fluid wave when PT prolonged) and 2% ascites with normal PT and no shifting dullness - PPVs, not sens/spec, so not entered. Status partially_quantified. This id duplicates exam_shifting_dullness in scope; the same evidence base was used.
